Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a deaf boy named Tom. Tom could not hear, but he was very good at seeing and feeling things. He had many friends who loved to play with him. They would play games like tag and hide-and-seek. Tom was very fast and good at finding his friends.
One day, the town bell would ring at noon. Everyone was excited to hear the bell, but Tom knew he could not hear it. He felt sad, but his friends had a plan. They decided to help Tom feel the bell ring too. They took Tom to the big bell and let him touch it while it rang. When the bell rang, Tom could feel the strong vibrations and he smiled.
The moral of the story is that even if someone is different or has a problem, like Tom being deaf, we can still find ways to help them and make them happy. We should always be kind and caring to everyone, no matter how different they are.

They ran inside the maze and followed the paths. Sometimes they turned left, sometimes they turned right. They saw many flowers and birds, but they did not see the exit. They started to feel lost and scared.
They heard a loud roar behind them. It was a big lion who lived in the maze. He was hungry and angry. He wanted to catch Tom and Lily and eat them.
Tom and Lily ran away from the lion. They looked for a place to hide. They saw a small hole in the bushes. They crawled inside and hoped the lion would not find them.
The lion came closer and closer. He smelled Tom and Lily in the hole. He reached his paw inside and tried to grab them. He pinched Lily's leg with his sharp claws. Lily cried out in pain.
Tom was brave and smart. He saw a stick on the ground. He picked it up and poked the lion's eye with it. The lion howled and backed away. He was hurt and afraid.
Tom and Lily saw their chance. They ran out of the hole and out of the maze. They found their mom and dad waiting for them. They hugged them and told them what happened. They were happy and safe. They never went back to the maze again.

Tim and Jen were twins who liked to play in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat, a scarf and a carrot nose. They named him Bob and gave him a hug.
"Bob is our friend," Tim said. "He will stay with us forever."
"No, he won't," Jen said. "He will melt when the sun comes out. Then he will be gone."
Tim did not like that. He wanted Bob to stay. He got angry at Jen. He threw a snowball at her. Jen threw one back. They started to fight.
"Stop it, you two!" Mom said. She came out of the house. She saw Bob and smiled. "What a nice snowman you made. But you should not fight. Fighting is bad."
"Jen said Bob will melt," Tim said. "I don't want him to melt. I want him to stay."
"Tim, Jen is right," Mom said. "Bob will melt sooner or later. That's what happens to snow. But you can always make another one. And you can take a picture of Bob to remember him."
Tim and Jen did not like that. They did not want another snowman. They wanted Bob. They did not want a picture. They wanted Bob. They cried and hugged Bob.
But Mom was right. The next day, the sun came out. It was warm and bright. Bob started to melt. His hat fell off. His scarf slipped. His carrot nose dropped. His chubby body got smaller and smaller. Tim and Jen watched and cried. Bob was gone. They had no friend. They had no snowman. They had nothing. They were sad.

Once upon a time, in a deep, deep forest, there lived a rabbit and a bear. They were good friends and liked to play together. One day, they decided to play a game called "freeze."
"Let's take turns," said the rabbit. "When I say 'freeze,' you stop moving. When you say 'freeze,' I stop moving."

"I don't know. Let's find out," Ben said.
They opened the box and saw many smaller boxes inside. They had holes and flaps and strings. They looked like a maze.
"Wow, this is cool. Let's make a maze with the boxes," Lily said.
They took out the boxes and arranged them on the floor. They made a long and twisty maze with many turns and dead ends. They crawled inside and explored the maze. They had fun finding each other and hiding and making noises.
They did not hear their mom come home. She walked into the living room and saw the mess. She was grumpy.
"What are you doing? Look at this mess. You are not supposed to open that box. It is for the charity sale," she said.
Lily and Ben came out of the maze. They looked at their mom. They were sorry.
"We are sorry, mom. We were bored. We wanted to play. We discovered a maze in the box. It was fun," Lily said.
Ben nodded. He said, "We are sorry, mom. We did not know. We will help you clean up."
Their mom sighed. She was not so grumpy anymore. She saw that they were just curious and creative. She smiled.
"It's okay, kids. I understand. But next time, please ask me before you open a box. And please be careful with the boxes. They are for a good cause. Now, let's clean up and then we can have a snack. How about that?" she said.
Lily and Ben smiled. They said, "Okay, mom. Thank you, mom. We love you, mom."
They hugged their mom and helped her clean up the maze. They learned a lesson and had a snack. They were happy.

She liked to smell the sweet aroma of the cake as it baked. But most of all, she liked to taste the cake when it was done.
One day, Anna decided to bake a cake by herself. She wanted to surprise her mom and dad. She remembered the ingredients and the steps, but she did not measure them carefully. She put too much sugar, too little butter, and forgot the eggs. She also added some salt, pepper, and ketchup, because she thought they would make the cake more colorful and spicy.
When the cake was ready, Anna took it out of the oven and put it on a plate. She was very proud of her work. She called her mom and dad to the kitchen and said, "Look, I made a cake for you! Do you want to taste it?"
Her mom and dad smiled and thanked her for her effort. They each took a small bite of the cake and tried not to make a face. The cake was very sweet, very dry, and very weird. They did not like it at all, but they did not want to hurt Anna's feelings.
They said, "Wow, Anna, this is a very...interesting cake. You are very creative and brave to try new things. But you know, sometimes it is better to follow a recipe and measure the ingredients. That way, the cake will be more delicious and more balanced. Do you want to learn how to bake a cake with us next time?"
Anna nodded and said, "Yes, please. I want to learn how to bake a cake like you. I'm sorry, I did not mean to make a bad cake. I just wanted to make you happy."
Her mom and dad hugged her and said, "We are happy, Anna, because you are our daughter and we love you. You are very intelligent and kind, and we are proud of you. But remember, not everything that looks good tastes good. And not everyone who tastes your cake will be as nice as us. Some people might be mean and judge you. So, be careful and listen to your mom and dad, okay?"
Anna said, "Okay, mom and dad. I love you too. And I love cake. Can we bake a cake together now?"
They said, "Of course, Anna. Let's bake a cake together. And let's taste it together too."
The end.

The fisherman heard Sam and rowed his boat to the shore. He said, "Hello, little boy! I'm glad you like my fish. Do you want to see them?" He opened a basket and showed Sam his catch. There were three fish in the basket. One was big, one was medium, and one was tiny.
Sam looked at the fish and said, "Wow, you have a lot of fish! The big one is very big, the medium one is very medium, and the tiny one is very tiny. You are a good fisherman!"

Sam took the plate and the fork. He said, "Thank you, fisherman. You are very nice. I will enjoy my fish. But I have to hurry. My mom is waiting for me at home. She will be worried if I am late."
The fisherman said, "You're welcome, little boy. I understand. You have to go home. But come back tomorrow and we can fish again. Maybe we will catch more fish. Maybe we will catch a bigger fish. Maybe we will catch a fish that can speed in the water."
Sam said, "That sounds fun, fisherman. I will come back tomorrow and we can fish again. Maybe we will catch a fish that can speed in the water. That would be amazing. Goodbye, fisherman. See you tomorrow."

Just then, a tiny ant walked by and saw Tim and the robot. The ant said, "I can help you!" The ant walked up to the ball and, with a big push, the ball moved! Tim was so surprised. The ant was so small, but it was very strong. Tim learned that even small things can be useful and strong. And they all played happily together.

Tom and Lily are playing with blocks. They have many blocks of different shapes and colors. They like to build towers and houses with them.
"Look, I made a big tower!" Tom says. He shows Lily his tower of red and blue blocks. It is very tall and has a circle on top.
"Wow, that is nice!" Lily says. She likes Tom's tower, but she wants to make something different. She has a yellow and green block in her hand. It is not a circle, it is a square.
"I want to put this on your tower," Lily says. She tries to put the square on the circle, but it does not fit. It falls down and makes a loud noise.
"Hey, don't do that!" Tom says. He is angry. He does not want Lily to ruin his tower. He pushes Lily away and grabs the square.
"No, this is mine!" Lily says. She is sad. She wants to play with Tom, but he does not share. She pulls the square and tries to take it back.
They both pull and tug on the block. They do not see that their tower is shaking. It is about to fall.
"Stop, stop!" a voice says. It is Mom. She sees the children fighting and the tower wobbling. She runs to them and catches the tower before it crashes.
"Tom, Lily, what are you doing?" Mom says. She is not happy. She does not like to see them fight. She puts the tower on the floor and looks at them.
"Sorry, Mom," Tom and Lily say. They feel bad. They know they were wrong.
"Can you say sorry to each other?" Mom says. She wants them to be nice and make up.
"Sorry, Tom," Lily says. She gives him the square. She does not need it. She can find another block.
"Sorry, Lily," Tom says. He gives her the circle. He does not mind. He can use another block.
They hug and smile. They are friends again.
"Good, now can you play nicely?" Mom says. She is glad. She likes to see them happy.
"Yes, Mom," Tom and Lily say. They nod and look at their blocks.
They have an idea. They can make something together. They can use the circle and the square and the other blocks. They can make an open house. They can put the circle on the door and the square on the window. They can invite Mom to see their house.
They start to build. They are having fun. They are playing with blocks.

Once upon a time there were two children, a brother and a sister, out kayaking together on a quiet lake.
"Watch out!" shouted the brother, as his kayak bumped against the sister's.
Suddenly, a loud noise filled the air, and everything around them seemed to freeze. The brother and sister couldn't move.
"What's happening?" asked the sister.
The brother squinted in the direction of the noise. "There's a big bird over there," he said.
They looked up and saw a huge, white bird hovering in the sky, looking down at them.
The bird flew away and the spell was broken. The brother and sister continued paddling on the quiet lake, and all was as it should be.

"Hello!" he yelled gleefully. The man stopped and looked at him.
"Ugh," he said, "Get away from me, bird."
The parrot flew away, feeling sad and rejected. He wanted to make friends but it seemed like the rough man didn't want that.
The next day, the parrot spotted the same man walking down the street again. He flew over, determined to make friends this time. He was surprised to see the man pick up a rock and throw it at him.
The rock hit the parrot and he fell to the ground. He didn't move. The man turned and walked away, not recognizing what he had just done.
The parrot never flew again. He lay on the path, lifeless, with no one to recognize him.

"Let me see!" Lily said, grabbing the sheep from Tom. She pressed the button on its ear. The sheep made a sound. "Baa, baa, baa!"
Tom and Lily laughed. They liked the sheep. They decided to name it Fluffy.
"Can we keep Fluffy?" Lily asked.
"Sure, why not?" Tom said. "He is our new friend."

"Hey, Lily, let's record Fluffy!" Tom said.
"Record Fluffy? How?" Lily asked.
"Watch me!" Tom said. He took Fluffy and the record player. He pressed the button on Fluffy's ear and the record button on the player at the same time. Fluffy said, "Baa, baa, baa!" and the player recorded it.
"Wow, that's cool!" Lily said.
Tom pressed the play button on the player. Fluffy's voice came out. "Baa, baa, baa!"
Tom and Lily laughed again. They liked to hear Fluffy's voice. They recorded Fluffy many times. They made him say different things. They made him say, "Hello, I am Fluffy!" and "I love Tom and Lily!" and "I am a happy sheep!"
They had a lot of fun with Fluffy and the record player. They played with them until it was time for dinner. They put Fluffy and the record player back in the box. They hugged Fluffy and said goodbye.
"See you tomorrow, Fluffy!" Tom said.
"We love you, Fluffy!" Lily said.
Fluffy smiled and said, "Baa, baa, baa!"

One day, John went for a walk in a very hot place. It was so hot that he was sweating and scratching an itch on his arm. Then he heard someone talk.
John stopped to listen. It was an old man's voice and he was saying, "Beware, it's a dangerous path ahead!" But John was curious and he wanted to know what was so dangerous, so he decided to keep walking.
As he kept walking, the heat got even hotter and the itch on his arm got worse. Finally, he reached the end of the path and he saw the old man. But he was too late to learn why the old man had warned him - a giant fire was about to engulf John!
John screamed for help but the fire was too big and too hot. He was never seen again.
The old man had been right - he should have listened!

But then, the beetle starts to move. It wants to get out of the box. It makes a noise. It flaps its wings.
"Look, the beetle is awake," Tom says. "It wants to go home. We should let it go."
"Yes, you are right," Sam says. "We had fun with the beetle, but it is not ours. It belongs to the park. We should say thank you and goodbye."
They open the box. They hold the beetle gently. They say thank you and goodbye. They watch the beetle fly away. They smile and wave.
They are still friends. They are still rich. They have each other. And they have a memory.

Sam and Mia were playing in the park. They saw a big bottle on the grass. It was shiny and blue. They ran to the bottle and picked it up.
"Look, it has a cork!" Sam said. "Maybe there is something inside."
"Let's open it and see!" Mia said. She tried to pull the cork, but it was too tight. She could not make it move.
"Here, let me try!" Sam said. He took the bottle from Mia and pushed the cork with his thumb. He pushed hard and hard, until the cork popped out.
"Wow, you did it!" Mia said. She looked inside the bottle. There was nothing but air.
"Maybe it's magic!" Sam said. "Maybe we can make a wish!"
"Okay, let's try!" Mia said. She closed her eyes and said, "I wish for a big cake!"
Sam closed his eyes and said, "I wish for a new bike!"
They opened their eyes and waited. But nothing happened. The bottle was still empty.
"That's not fair!" Sam said. He was angry. He threw the bottle on the ground. It broke into many pieces.
"Hey, don't do that!" Mia said. She was scared. She saw a man coming towards them. He was wearing a uniform and a hat. He looked angry too.
"Who are you?" Sam asked.
"I'm the park ranger," the man said. "And you are in big trouble. Do you know what you did? You released a rare bird that was in that bottle. It was part of a conservation project. Now it's gone and we can't find it. You also littered the park with glass. That's very dangerous and bad for the environment. You should be ashamed of yourselves."
Sam and Mia felt very sorry. They did not know about the bird. They did not mean to be bad. They wanted to say sorry, but they could not find the words. They started to cry.
The man shook his head. He took them by the hand and led them to his car. He said he would take them to their parents and tell them what they did. He said they would have to pay a fine and do some community service. He said they would learn their lesson.
Sam and Mia wished they never found the bottle. They wished they never made a wish. They wished they could go back and do things differently. But it was too late. They had made a big mistake. And they had to face the consequences.

The moral of the story is: Don't be greedy and dishonest. Listen to your mom and respect your animals. They are your friends and they care for you.

Anna said, "Someone took my flute. I can't find it. It was my favorite thing. I want it back."
Lily felt sorry for Anna. She said, "Don't weep. Maybe I can help you. Let's look for your flute together."

Anna was happy. She said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very kind. You helped me find my flute."
Lily said, "You're welcome, Anna. I'm glad you have your flute back. Can I play with it too?"
Anna said, "Yes, you can. I'm sorry I was mean to you before. I learned that sharing is good. Sharing makes friends."
They played the flute together and had fun.
The moral of the story is: Sharing is good. Sharing makes friends.

"But Mom, we love pizza!" Tom said. "Pizza is yummy and cheesy and round. Soup and salad are boring and green and wet."
Mom shook her head. "Pizza is not healthy. It has too much fat and salt. Soup and salad have vitamins and fiber. They make you strong and smart. You can have pizza once in a while, but not every day."
Tom and Lily did not like Mom's answer. They made sad faces and crossed their arms. They did not want to eat soup and salad. They wanted to eat pizza.
Dad came home from work. He saw Tom and Lily's sad faces. He asked them what was wrong. They told him that Mom said no pizza for dinner.
Dad looked at Mom. He smiled. He said, "I have a surprise for you. I brought pizza for dinner!"
Tom and Lily's eyes lit up. They jumped up and down. They cheered. They hugged Dad. They said, "Yay! Pizza! Pizza! Pizza!"
Mom looked at Dad. She frowned. She said, "You brought pizza? But I made soup and salad. I told them pizza was not good for them."
Dad shrugged. He said, "I know, I know. But pizza is fun and tasty and easy. Soup and salad are good for you, but they can wait for another day. Sometimes, you have to treat yourself and your family. Don't worry, we'll eat healthy tomorrow."
Mom sighed. She said, "You're right, you're right. Pizza is fun and tasty and easy. And you're a good dad and a wise husband. I love you."
She kissed Dad. She said, "Okay, let's eat pizza. But only one slice each. And we'll have some salad too."
Tom and Lily did not care. They were happy. They had pizza for dinner. They thanked Dad. They said, "You're the best dad ever!"
They ate pizza and salad. They were full and satisfied. They had a good night. They learned that sometimes, pizza is okay. And sometimes, Mom and Dad are wise.

It's dangerous. The engine might start and go away. You have to stay with me." Lily was sad. She wanted to touch the engine, and hear it, and smell it. She thought her mom was mean.
Lily waited until her mom was busy. She saw a man with a hat and a whistle. He was the driver of the engine. He was talking to another man. Lily saw her chance. She sneaked to the engine, and climbed inside. She saw many buttons and levers. She remembered some of them from her book. She wanted to try them. She was very naughty.
She pushed a button, and the engine made a loud noise. She pulled a lever, and the engine moved. She was scared, but also excited. She felt like she was in her book. She didn't see the driver running to the engine, or the people shouting, or the other trains on the tracks. She only saw the engine going faster and faster.
The driver managed to get inside the engine. He saw Lily in the seat. He was angry, but also worried. He grabbed Lily, and put her on his lap. He tried to stop the engine, but it was too late. The engine crashed into another train. There was a big bang, and a lot of smoke. Lily and the driver were hurt. They had to go to the hospital. Lily was very sorry. She learned a hard lesson. Tom and Lily were very happy. They were going on a holiday with Mum and Dad. They packed their bags and got in the car. They drove for a long time and saw many things. They saw cows and sheep and trees and flowers.
They arrived at a big house near the sea. It was their holiday home. They ran inside and chose their rooms. Tom picked a room with a big bed and a window. Lily picked a room with a small bed and a shelf. On the shelf, there was a toy. It was a orange dinosaur. Lily liked dinosaurs. She took the toy and hugged it.
"Look, Tom, I found a dinosaur!" Lily said.
"Wow, that's cool!" Tom said. "Can I see it?"
Lily gave the toy to Tom. He looked at it and pressed a button. The toy made a loud roar. Tom and Lily laughed. But then, something strange happened. The toy started to shrink. It became smaller and smaller until it was the size of a coin.
"Tom, what did you do?" Lily cried.
"I don't know!" Tom said. "I just pressed the button!"
They tried to press the button again, but nothing happened. The toy was too small. They could barely see it.
"Mum, Dad, help!" Tom and Lily shouted.
Mum and Dad came to their room. They saw the tiny toy on the floor.
"What happened?" Mum asked.
"The dinosaur shrank!" Lily said.
"How did that happen?" Dad asked.
"Tom pressed the button!" Lily said.
"I'm sorry, Lily," Tom said. "I didn't mean to."
Mum and Dad looked at the toy. They saw a label on it. It said: "Shrink-o-saur. The toy that shrinks when you press the button. Fun for all ages. Batteries not included."
"Oh, dear," Mum said. "This is a very silly toy. Who would make such a thing?"
"I don't know," Dad said. "But maybe we can find a way to make it big again."
They took the toy and went to the kitchen. They looked for something that could make it grow. They tried water, milk, bread, honey, and salt. But nothing worked. The toy stayed small.
"Maybe we should just leave it alone," Mum said. "Maybe it will grow back by itself."
"Or maybe we can buy a new one," Dad said. "A bigger one. A better one."
Tom and Lily felt sad. They liked the orange dinosaur. They didn't want a new one. They wanted the old one.
"Can we keep it?" Lily asked.
"Of course, you can," Mum said. "But you have to be very careful. It's very small. You might lose it."
Tom and Lily nodded. They put the toy in a box. They made a bed for it with cotton and paper. They gave it a name. They called it Tiny.
They hoped that Tiny would grow back. But they also loved it as it was. They played with it every day. They took it to the beach, to the park, to the shops. They showed it to their friends. They told them the story of how it shrank.
They had a lot of fun with Tiny. They had a good holiday. They never forgot the orange dinosaur.

But then, something unexpected happened. The ball rolled into a big hole! It was stuck and could not get out. The small girl saw the ball and said, "I will help you, ball." She pulled the ball out of the hole. The ball was very happy and said, "Thank you, girl. I will be more careful now." From that day on, the ball was not careless anymore. It learned to roll and play without making trouble.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lucy. She had a pretty skirt with stars on it. Lucy loved her skirt very much. She wore it every day.
One sunny day, Lucy went to the park. She saw a deaf dog named Spot. Spot could not hear, but he was very good at playing. Lucy said, "Hi Spot! Do you like my skirt?" Spot wagged his tail and smiled. Lucy knew that meant he liked her skirt.
As the sun began to set, the stars on Lucy's skirt started to shine. Lucy and Spot played under the shiny stars until it was time to go home. They were very happy to be friends.

One day, a little girl named Lucy wanted to make soup. She asked her mom, "Can I make soup, please?" Her mom said, "Yes, but be careful."
Lucy started to make the soup. She put in some harsh things like a rock and a stick. Her brother Tom saw it and said, "That's not good soup!" Lucy was sad.
Tom said, "Let's guess what we need to make good soup." They took out the rock and stick. They put in nice things like carrots and peas. They made the soup together and it was yummy.
The moral value of the story is that we should work together and help each other to make things better.

One day, a little girl named Sue went to the park with her mom. Sue saw a big orange cat sitting on the grass. The cat was very pretty, and Sue wanted to play with it. She ran to the cat and said, "Hi, cat! Let's play!"
The cat looked at Sue and said, "I lost my tooth. Can you help me find it?" Sue wanted to help her new friend. They both looked around the park, under the trees and near the swings.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes they missed the ball and it rolled away. Then they had to chase it before it went too far.
One time, the ball rolled near a big road. Lily and Ben ran after it, but they did not look for cars. A loud horn made them stop and look. A big truck was coming fast. It had black smoke coming out of its back. The smoke smelled bad and made Lily and Ben cough.
"Stop!" shouted a voice. It was their mom. She had seen them run to the road. She was scared and angry. She ran to them and grabbed their hands. She pulled them away from the road and the truck. She slapped their legs and said, "No! No! No! You don't run to the road! The road is dangerous! You could get hurt by the cars! You have to look and listen before you cross the road! Do you understand?"
Lily and Ben nodded. They felt sorry and scared. They did not like the slap or the smoke or the horn. They hugged their mom and said, "Sorry, mom. We won't do it again. We love you, mom."
Their mom hugged them back and said, "I love you too, Lily and Ben. But you have to be careful and follow the rules. The road is not a place to play. The park is a place to play. Let's go back to the park and play with the ball. But first, let's wash our faces and hands. The smoke made them dirty."
Lily and Ben agreed. They followed their mom back to the park. They washed their faces and hands in a fountain. They felt better. They saw their ball. It was still on the grass, not too far from the road. They picked it up and kicked it to each other. They laughed and had fun. They did not go near the road again. They saw the truck go away. It was distant and small. They did not care about it. They only cared about their mom and their ball. They were happy.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Ann went to the store with her mom. They wanted to buy some interesting things for their home. On their way, they saw a big clock. The clock went "strike, strike, strike!" Ann looked at her mom and said, "Mommy, what is that sound?"
Her mom smiled and said, "That is the clock telling us it is three o'clock, Ann. It is time for us to go home and have some coffee!"
When they got home, Ann's mom made some hot coffee for herself and gave Ann a cup of warm milk. They sat down at the table and talked about their day. Ann told her mom about the interesting things she saw at the store and how she liked the sound of the clock.
Ann's mom laughed and said, "Yes, the clock has a lovely sound when it strikes. Maybe one day we can get a clock like that for our home." Ann nodded and smiled, happy to have a fun day with her mom.

One day, a little girl named Sally went outside to play. It was a gloomy day, but Sally didn't mind. She liked to play in the dirt and make mud pies. She brought her favorite toy, a pair of scissors, with her.
Sally saw her friend Timmy playing in his yard. "Hi Timmy!" she called. "Do you want to play with me?" Timmy smiled and said, "Yes, Sally! Let's play together!" They decided to play a game of hide and seek.
Sally had an idea. "I'll bury my scissors in the dirt, and you try to find them!" she said. Timmy agreed and started counting. Sally quickly buried her scissors and hid behind a tree. When Timmy finished counting, he looked all around for the scissors.
After a while, Timmy found the scissors in the dirt. "I found them, Sally!" he shouted. Sally came out from behind the tree and clapped her hands. They both laughed and decided to play some more games together. Even though the day was gloomy, Sally and Timmy had a lot of fun playing outside.

Once there was a big, impressive tree. It was very tall and strong. But one day, a small leak came from the tree. A tiny bug saw the leak and went to tell his friend.
"Look! The big tree has a leak," said the tiny bug to his friend. "It might rot if we don't help it."
The two tiny bugs knew they had to do something. They went to the tree and tried to fix the leak. But they were too small to fix it alone. They needed help from their friends. So, they asked more bugs to join them.
Many bugs came to help the big tree. They all worked together to fix the leak. The tree was happy and thanked the bugs. The bugs were happy too because they saved the tree from rotting.
The moral of the story is: when we work together, we can fix big problems.

Sam likes to play with his toy motorcycle. He makes it zoom and vroom on the floor. He pretends he is a big rider. He likes the red and blue colors of his motorcycle. He thinks it is very pretty.
One day, his cousin Lily comes to visit. She sees his motorcycle and wants to play with it too. She asks Sam, "Can I have a turn?" Sam does not want to share. He says, "No, it is mine!" He holds his motorcycle tight.
Lily is sad. She says, "Please, Sam, just for a little bit. I like your motorcycle. It is so pretty." Sam still does not want to share. He says, "No, go away!" He turns his back to Lily.
Lily feels angry. She tries to grab his motorcycle. She says, "Give it to me!" Sam resists. He says, "No, stop it!" They pull and tug on the motorcycle. They start to cry.
Mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees them fighting over the motorcycle. She says, "What is going on here? Why are you not sharing?" Sam and Lily look at Mom. They feel ashamed. They say, "Sorry, Mom."
Mom says, "It is okay to say sorry, but you also need to learn to share. Sharing is caring. How about you take turns playing with the motorcycle? You can each have five minutes. Then you can switch. Does that sound fair?" Sam and Lily nod. They say, "Okay, Mom."
Mom smiles. She says, "Good. Now, let's play nicely. Who wants to go first?" Sam says, "Me!" Lily says, "Me too!" Mom says, "How about we flip a coin? Heads, Sam goes first. Tails, Lily goes first. Ready?" Sam and Lily say, "Yes!" Mom flips the coin. It lands on heads. Sam says, "Yay!" Lily says, "Aw!" Mom says, "Don't worry, Lily. You will have your turn soon. Sam, you have five minutes. Then you have to give the motorcycle to Lily. Okay?" Sam says, "Okay." He plays with his motorcycle. He says, "Zoom, vroom!" Lily watches. She waits for her turn. She says, "It is so pretty."

"I saw it first!" Lily said.
"No, I did!" Ben said.
They pulled on the radish from both sides, trying to get it out. They started to quarrel and shout at each other.
"Let go, it's mine!" Lily said.
"No, it's mine!" Ben said.
They pulled so hard that the radish snapped in half. They both fell back on the grass, holding their pieces. They looked at the radish and felt sad. It was not as nice as they thought. It was dirty and bitter and had a hole in it.
They looked at each other and felt sorry. They did not want to quarrel and hurt their friend. They wanted to share and have fun.
"I'm sorry, Lily," Ben said.
"I'm sorry, Ben," Lily said.
They hugged and made up. They threw away the radish and decided to play something else. They found a ball and a hoop and had a great time. They were happy and forgot about the radish. They were friends again.

Spot tried to find another way to get the meat. He climbed up a tree near the house and jumped onto the roof. But he slipped and fell down. Spot was hurt and still very hungry. He did not get the meat and the people were still upset with him.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his sheet. He would run and jump and fetch the sheet all day long. Spot's best friend was a little boy named Tim. Tim and Spot played together every day.
One day, Spot and Tim were playing with the sheet in the park. A big, mean dog came up and wanted to play too. The big dog said, "Give me the sheet!" He was very demanding. Spot didn't want to give up his sheet, but the big dog was very big and scary.
Spot tried to be brave and said, "No, this is my sheet!" But the big dog didn't listen. He took the sheet from Spot and ran away. Spot and Tim were very sad. They went home without their sheet and never saw it again.

At the safari, Mommy paid for the tickets. They went to the zoo part of the safari. There were lots of animals to see. Lily was very busy looking at the animals and taking pictures.
She saw a giraffe. It was so tall! Then she saw a zebra. It had black and white stripes. There were also lots of monkeys swinging around in the trees.
Later, they went to the amusement part of the safari. Mommy paid for Lily to go on all the fun rides. They went on a train, a roller coaster and a ferris wheel.
The safari was so much fun! Lily was very tired after a long day of being busy, but she had a smile on her face. It was the best day ever!

One sunny day, Andy and his mom walked in the woods. Andy was curious and wanted to explore everything. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise coming from the nearby bushes. Andy's mom grabbed his hand and said, "Let's follow it."
They walked a bit and saw a baby animal - it was a prune. Its big eyes looked curiously at the two of them. Andy's mom said, "It's a baby prune. Let's take it home and take care of it." Andy wanted to keep it, so he nodded and smiled.
On the way home, the prune was running in the woods, and Andy and his mom were following it. They soon made it home and the prune followed them inside.
Andy and his mom were happy to have the prune as a pet and they named it Pruney. From that day forward, Andy and Pruney were the best of friends. Pruney liked to explore and follow Andy everywhere he went - even around the whole world.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She lived near a big lake. One day, Mia saw a kayak on the lake. She wanted to try it.
Mia went to her mom and asked if she could go in the kayak. Her mom said yes, but she needed to speak to her dad first. Mia went to her dad and told him about the kayak. Her dad said it was okay, but she needed to be careful.
Mia went back to the lake and got in the kayak. She paddled around and had lots of fun. But then, she saw something in the water. It was a big, disgusting fish! Mia didn't like the fish, so she paddled away. She went back to her mom and dad and told them about her adventure. Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. They have many cars, big and small, red and blue, fast and slow. They like to race them on the floor.
One day, Mom says, "It is time to go to the park. You can bring one car each. Choose your car and put on your shoes."
Lily and Ben run to their toy box. They look at all the cars. Lily picks a big red car. She likes how it makes noise and has lights. Ben picks a small blue car. He likes how it is smooth and shiny.
They put on their shoes and go to the door. Mom takes their hands and they walk to the car. Lily and Ben put their cars on the seat next to them.
At the park, they see a big hill. They want to race their cars down the hill. They run to the top and get ready.
"Ready, set, go!" Lily says. She pushes her big red car. It goes fast and loud. Ben pushes his small blue car. It goes slow and quiet.
Lily's car reaches the bottom first. She cheers and claps. "I win, I win! My car is the best!"
Ben's car stops halfway. He frowns and sighs. "My car is stupid. It is too slow."
Lily runs to Ben and hugs him. "No, your car is not stupid. It is just different. I like your car. It is smooth and shiny. Do you want to trade?"
Ben smiles and nods. "Yes, I want to trade. Thank you, Lily. You are a good sister."
They trade their cars and race again. This time, Ben's car wins. He cheers and claps. "I win, I win! Your car is the best!"
Lily's car stops halfway. She laughs and shrugs. "My car is not the best. It is just different. I like your car. It makes noise and has lights. Do you want to trade back?"
Ben smiles and nods. "Yes, I want to trade back. Thank you, Lily. You are a good sister."
They trade their cars back and hug. They play with their cars until Mom says, "It is time to go home. You had fun with your cars. You are good twins."
Lily and Ben say, "Yes, we had fun. We are good twins. We love our cars. We love each other." They put their cars in their pockets and hold Mom's hands. They go back to the car and go home.

"Wow, you look like a princess, Lily. Can I try?" Mia asks. She grabs the lipstick from Lily and puts some on her mouth too.
But Mia puts too much. The lipstick goes out of her lips and onto her cheeks and nose. She looks like a clown.
"Hey, give it back! You are wasting it!" Lily says. She tries to take the lipstick from Mia, but Mia holds it tight.
"No, it's mine! I want to play with it!" Mia says. She pushes Lily away.
Lily gets angry. She strikes Mia on the arm. Mia cries out and strikes Lily back. They start to fight and pull each other's hair.
Mom hears the noise and comes into the room. She sees the girls fighting and the makeup all over their faces and clothes. She is shocked and angry.
"What are you doing? This is not how you play with makeup! This is not how you treat your sister! You are both in big trouble!" Mom says. She takes the makeup bag and the lipstick from the girls. She makes them clean up and say sorry to each other.
Lily and Mia feel bad. They hug and apologize. They promise to not play with mom's makeup again.
Mom forgives them and gives them a hug too. She says they can have some yummy cookies as a snack. The girls are happy and go to the kitchen. They decide to play with something else next time.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is brown and fluffy. It has a long tail and a wet nose.
"Can we touch the dog?" Lily asks Tom.
"I don't know. Maybe we should ask the owner first," Tom says.
They look around and see a man sitting on a bench. He is reading a book. He has a leash in his hand. The leash is attached to the dog.
"Excuse me, sir. Can we touch your dog?" Lily says.
The man looks up and smiles. He sees Lily and Tom. They are cute and polite.
"Sure, you can touch my dog. His name is Rover. He is very friendly and loves children," the man says.
Lily and Tom walk towards the dog. They reach out their hands and touch his fur. It is soft and warm. The dog wags his tail and licks their faces. Lily and Tom giggle.
"Hello, Rover. You are a nice dog," Lily says.
"You are a good boy," Tom says.
They pet the dog and play with him. They throw a ball and he fetches it. They rub his belly and he rolls over. They have fun.
But then, they smell something smelly. It is coming from the dog. They pinch their noses and make a face.
"Yuck! What is that smell?" Lily says.
"I think he rolled in something bad," Tom says.
They look at the dog and see some dirt and grass on his fur. They also see some poop.
"Ew! He rolled in poop!" Lily says.
"That's gross!" Tom says.
They run away from the dog and back to the man. They tell him what happened.
"Oh, no! Rover, you naughty dog! You need a bath!" the man says.
He apologizes to Lily and Tom. He says he will take the dog home and clean him. He thanks them for playing with him.
Lily and Tom say goodbye to the man and the dog. They are still friends. They are not mad at the dog. They know he did not mean to be smelly. They hope to see him again. But next time, they hope he will be clean.

The bird, the tree, and the house were very happy together. They watched the sun rise and set every day. Even when the wind blew hard and the tree was dangerous, they were safe and happy together. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a small town, lived a clever boy named Tim. Tim loved to write poems. One day, he wrote a new poem and wanted to share it with his friend, Sam.
Tim ran to Sam's house and said, "Sam, I wrote a new poem! Would you like to hear it?" Sam looked at the sky and said, "It looks like rain, but I will listen." So, Tim read his poem to Sam. But while Tim was reading, it started to rain. Sam started to complain, "I don't like the rain! It's wet and cold!"
Tim wanted to help Sam feel better, so he said, "Let's go inside my house and I will read my poem again." They went inside, but the rain got worse. Water started to come in Tim's house. Tim and Sam tried to stop the water, but they could not. The water ruined Tim's poem and made a big mess in the house.
In the end, Tim and Sam were sad because the rain had ruined their day and Tim's poem. They learned that sometimes, even clever ideas can't stop bad things from happening.

Once there was a little bird. It was so excited, 'cause it wanted to soar free in the sky. But, it was a bit scared too. It looked at the tall pole. It was so high up, and seemed really hard to climb.
The little bird took a deep breath and started to flap its wings. Then, it hopped up to the top of the pole! It was so proud of itself!
Once up on the pole, it spread its wings. They felt so good and light. Then, with one big jump, the bird soared up and away into the sky! It was so happy and its little heart beat so fast.
Up in the sky, the clouds were soft and fluffy. And the air smelled a bit sour too, like apples. But the little bird didn't care. It just kept soaring, free and happy in the sky, until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Anna. One morning, Anna woke up feeling very nervous. She had to take the subway to meet her friends at the park. Anna had never been on a subway before and she was really scared. She asked her mom if she could go with her, but her mom said no.
So Anna put on her coat and walked to the subway station. She stepped on to the train and sat down. At first, the ride went smoothly, but then it got slower and slower. When the train stopped, all the passengers had to get off and walk. Anna wasn't sure where to go, so she followed the other passengers.
After walking for a long time, she ended up at an old, dark station. It was creepy and Anna was very frightened. Suddenly, a group of thugs appeared out of the shadows and surrounded her. They started to steal her things and she felt helpless.
Anna was so scared that she passed out. When she woke up, she was alone in the dark train station. All of her things were gone. Anna was so shaken up, she was never able to take the subway again.

Once upon a time, in a big yellow house, there lived a sad little girl. She would often weep because she felt lonely. She had no friends to play with and her toys were old and broken.
One day, while she was crying, a yellow bird flew into her room. The bird had a special power. It could make her toys new again. The little girl was very surprised and happy. She stopped weeping and started to play with her toys.

Sara and Tom were playing in the yard. They saw a big bird with brown feathers and a red thing on its head. Sara said, "Look, Tom, a turkey!"
Tom said, "No, Sara, that is not a turkey. That is a chicken."
Sara said, "How do you know, Tom? Did you ask the bird?"
Tom said, "No, I did not ask the bird. I just guess. I know what a turkey looks like. A turkey has a big tail that opens like a fan. This bird does not have a big tail."
Sara said, "Maybe this bird is a baby turkey. Maybe its tail will grow bigger when it gets older."
Tom said, "No, Sara, you are wrong. This bird is a chicken. I am sure."
Sara and Tom started to argue. They did not agree on what the bird was. They did not listen to each other. They did not have fun.
Then, they heard a voice from the house. It was Mom. She said, "Sara, Tom, come inside. It is time for lunch. I made you a sandwich with turkey and cheese."
Sara and Tom ran to the house. They were hungry. They said, "Sorry, Mom, we were playing."
Mom said, "That is okay, my loves. But next time, try to be more honest with each other. If you are not sure about something, you can say, 'I think' or 'I wonder' instead of 'I know' or 'I guess'. That way, you can learn from each other and have more fun."
Sara and Tom nodded. They said, "Okay, Mom, we will try to be more honest. Thank you for the lunch. We love turkey and cheese."
Mom smiled. She said, "You are welcome, my loves. I love you too. Enjoy your lunch."

Kitty nodded and went back inside to warm up. From that day on, Kitty was happy to play in the warm sun and didn't feel envious of Rover anymore.

"Look at me, Tom!" Lily says. She sits on the slide. She is ready to go down.
But then she sees a white note on the slide. It has some words on it. Lily does not know what they mean. She picks up the note. She tries to read it.
"What is that, Lily?" Tom asks. He is curious. He wants to see the note too.
"I don't know, Tom. It is a note. It has words. But I can't read them." Lily says. She shows the note to Tom.
Tom looks at the note. He can't read it either. He thinks it is boring. He wants to slide.
"Let me see, Lily." Tom says. He tries to take the note from Lily.
But Lily does not want to give it to him. She thinks it is important. She wants to keep it.
"No, Tom. It is mine. I found it." Lily says. She holds the note tight.
Tom gets angry. He wants the note too. He pushes Lily.
Lily falls off the slide. She drops the note. She hurts her knee. She starts to cry.
Tom feels bad. He did not mean to hurt Lily. He picks up the note. He gives it back to Lily.
"I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I should not have pushed you." Tom says. He helps Lily get up.
Lily stops crying. She takes the note. She forgives Tom.
"It's okay, Tom. I'm sorry too. I should have shared with you." Lily says. She hugs Tom.
They are friends again. They decide to leave the note on the slide. Maybe someone else can read it. They go to play on the swings. They have fun.

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big bird fly in the sky. They want to fly too.
"Let's make wings with paper and dust!" Anna says. She finds some paper and dust on the ground. She sticks them together with glue.
"Look, I have wings!" Anna says. She puts them on her arms and runs. She tries to fly, but she falls.
"Ouch!" Anna says. She cries. Her wings are broken.
Ben laughs. He thinks Anna is silly. He says, "You can't fly with paper and dust. You need feathers and wind."
Anna is angry. She says, "You are mean. You don't know anything. Paper and dust are magic. They can make me fly."
Ben says, "No, they can't. You are lying. Show me how you fly."
Anna says, "Fine. I will show you. But you have to close your eyes."
Ben says, "OK. I will close my eyes. But you have to be quick."
Anna says, "OK. I will be quick." She closes her eyes too. She wishes very hard. She wants to fly.
She feels a mild breeze on her face. She feels light and free. She opens her eyes. She sees the sky and the clouds. She is flying!
She looks down. She sees Ben. He is still on the ground. He is still closing his eyes. He is waiting for her.
She smiles. She says, "Look, Ben. I am flying. I told you paper and dust are magic."
Ben hears her voice. He opens his eyes. He sees her in the air. He is shocked. He says, "Wow! How did you do that?"
Anna says, "I don't know. I just wished and believed. Do you want to fly with me?"
Ben says, "Yes, I do. I am sorry I laughed at you. You are not silly. You are amazing."
Anna says, "It's OK. I forgive you. Come on, let's fly together."
She flies down. She gives him a hug. She gives him some paper and dust. She says, "Put these on your arms. Close your eyes. Wish and believe. Then you can fly too."
Ben does what she says. He feels a mild breeze on his face. He feels light and free. He opens his eyes. He sees the sky and the clouds. He is flying!
He sees Anna. She is smiling. She says, "We did it! We are flying!"
They fly together. They have fun. They are happy. They are friends.

One day, they found a large glass in the kitchen. It was bigger than their heads, and shiny and clear. They wondered what they could pretend with it. Tom had an idea. He said, "Let's pretend this is a magic glass. It can show us anything we want to see."
Mia liked the idea. She said, "OK, what do you want to see?" Tom thought for a moment. He said, "I want to see a dinosaur. A big, scary dinosaur." He held the glass in front of his face and looked inside. He made a roar and said, "Look, there's a dinosaur. It's coming to get us. Run!"
Mia laughed and ran with him. She said, "My turn, my turn. I want to see a fairy. A pretty, sparkly fairy." She took the glass from Tom and looked inside. She made a tinkling sound and said, "Look, there's a fairy. She's flying to us. She wants to be our friend. Come!"
Tom smiled and followed her. They played with the glass for a long time, pretending to see different things. They had fun and forgot about everything else.
But they did not notice that their mom was watching them. She had a surprise for them. She had bought them a new book, with pictures of dinosaurs and fairies and many other things. She waited for them to finish playing, and then she said, "Tom, Mia, I have something for you. Come and see."
They ran to her and saw the book. They were very happy and excited. They said, "Wow, thank you, mom. This is the best book ever. Can you read it to us?"
Mom said, "Of course, I can. But first, let's put the glass back in the kitchen. It's not a toy, you know. It's for drinking juice or water."
Tom and Mia nodded. They said, "OK, mom. We're sorry. We were just pretending."
Mom said, "I know, and that's fine. Pretending is good. It helps you learn and have fun. But you also have to be careful and respectful with things that are not yours. Do you understand?"
Tom and Mia said, "Yes, mom. We understand. We love you."
Mom said, "I love you too. Now, let's go and read the book. I'm sure you'll find many more things to pretend with."

One day, Bob and Liz were playing outside. Liz was pushing Bob on the swing. It was really hot outside, and they were both sweating. Suddenly, Bob heard a loud sound coming from the tree in their yard. When they looked closer, they saw a dead bird lying on the ground.
Bob and Liz were both scared. They didn't know what to do. But then, Bob had an idea. He quickly grabbed a stick and started poking the bird with it. He wanted to see if it would move.
That's when the bird suddenly opened its eyes and started repeating the same thing over and over again - "hot, hot, hot!"
Bob and Liz were shocked. They had just awoken the dead bird with their stick! Bob quickly grabbed Liz and they ran inside the house.
From then on, Bob and Liz knew that it was important not to repeat the same thing over and over again.

"These must be someone's happy secrets," Daisy thought and smiled.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and find bugs and worms. They also liked to eat snacks that Mom gave them. Today, Mom gave them some crackers and cream. Cream was white and soft and yummy.
"Look, I found a big worm!" Tom said, holding a long, brown thing in his hand.
"Let me see!" Lily said, running to him. She saw the worm and made a face. "That's not a worm, Tom. That's a snake!"
"A snake?" Tom said, dropping it. "But it's not scary. It's not moving."
"That's because it's dead, Tom. It's rotting. That means it's old and bad and smelly. You don't want to touch it. It can make you sick."
"Yuck!" Tom said, wiping his hand on his shirt. "I don't like rotting things. They're gross."
"Me neither," Lily said. "Let's go eat our snacks. They're fresh and good and tasty."
They ran to the picnic blanket where Mom had left their snacks. They picked up their crackers and cream and took big bites. They smiled and chewed.
But they didn't notice that the cream had been in the sun for too long. It had turned sour and lumpy. It was rotting too.
Soon, they felt sick in their tummies. They spit out the cream and cried.
"Mom! Mom!" they called. "The cream is bad! It's rotting!"
Mom heard them and came running. She saw the cream and smelled it. She made a face too.
"Oh, no!" she said. "I'm sorry, kids. I forgot to put the cream in the cooler. It went bad in the heat. You shouldn't eat it. It can make you sick."
She hugged them and gave them some water to drink. She threw away the cream and the crackers.
"Are you okay?" she asked.
Lily and Tom nodded. They felt better after drinking the water. They learned their lesson.
They never ate rotting things again. They only ate fresh and good and tasty things.
And they stayed away from distant snakes.

Mommy hugged Sara and comforted her. She said, "I'm sorry, sweetie. The big kids are wrong. You are a smart and kind and beautiful girl. I love you very much. And so does your teddy bear. He is your best friend, right?"
Sara nodded and smiled a little. She hugged her teddy bear and said, "Yes, he is. He always listens to me and makes me feel better."
Mommy said, "That's good. You know, I have a surprise for you. Do you want to see it?"
Sara said, "Yes, please."
Mommy took Sara to the kitchen. There was a big cake on the table. It had pink frosting and sprinkles and candles. It said, "Happy Birthday, Sara!"
Sara gasped and clapped her hands. She said, "Wow! Is that for me?"
Mommy said, "Yes, it is. Today is your birthday, remember? You are four years old now. You are a big girl. And this is your treat. You can have a slice of cake and a glass of milk. And later, we can go to the park and play with your friends."
Sara was very happy. She said, "Thank you, Mommy. You are the best. I love you."
Mommy said, "I love you too, sweetie. Happy birthday."
They hugged and kissed and ate the cake. Sara felt much better. She was glad she had a modest but loving mommy and a loyal teddy bear. She was ready to face the big kids tomorrow. She knew she was not alone. She had a family and friends who cared for her. She was a lucky girl.

She wanted to write about the snake. She ran to her book and pens. She put the plug in the hole and the hole in the wall. She thought the snake would be happy. She did not know it was a bad snake.
The snake was not happy. It was angry. It did not like to be in the wall. It made a loud noise and a bright flash. It hurt Lily and her book and her pens. It burned them and broke them.
Lily screamed and cried. She dropped the snake and ran away. She was scared and sad. She did not hear her mom and dad come in. They saw the smoke and the fire and the snake. They saw Lily and her book and her pens. They were shocked and worried.
They called for Lily and tried to help her. But Lily did not hear them. She was deaf. The snake had made her deaf. She could not write anymore. She could not hear anymore. She had no stories and no pictures. She had nothing.

They dropped the bat and the ball and ran to the mailman. They said they were sorry and asked for the mail. The mailman gave them the envelope and told them to be more careful and respectful. He said he would talk to their mom and dad later.
Tim and Sam opened the envelope and saw the card and the gift. The card had a picture of their grandma and a big heart. It said, "I love you, Tim and Sam. You are my clever and sweet grandsons. Manny ran around the grounds, looking at each and every display that he could find. His mother watched with admiration, thankful for his little bursts of energy. At the very end of the grounds, Manny found a unique display. In the centre of a garden was a glass bulb filled with a beautiful glowing light. Suddenly, Manny ran forward, reaching out to grab the bulb.
"No, Manny!" his mother called out, moving quickly to grab him. But it was too late. Manny had already touched the bulb and it started spinning rapidly. Manny and his mother stepped back in shock.
The sound of an alarm filled the air and the museum guards ran towards them. In a voice that was surprisingly calm, the chief guard explained that the bulb was part of a special display to show what happened when things weren't handled with care.

Once upon a time, there was a poor farmer called Bill. He worked all day in the fields, planting seeds and sowing crops to feed his family. But one day, Bill noticed a big patch of weeds in the middle of his field. He sighed, for weeds meant that the crops would be harder to harvest.
Bill called his children to his side, and explained that he wanted them to help him with the weeds. His children were tired and wanted to play, but they could see how tired and worried Bill was, so they agreed.
The children worked all day, and soon, the patch of weeds was gone. Bill smiled and thanked his children, and they all went back home to have dinner.
The moral of the story is that we can all do our part to help, even if it feels like we have too much work to do. Bill felt too poor to hire more workers, but his children showed him that even they could make a difference.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy really wanted to try riding a bike. One day, Daddy gave Daisy a pedal bike. Daisy was so happy and couldn't wait to try it out.
Daddy was helping Daisy to push her bike. Daisy hopped on and tried to use her feet to pedal it. But Daisy wasn't strong enough and couldn't even move the pedals.
"I can't do it, Daddy!" Daisy cried, disappointed.
"Don't be sad, Daisy! If you keep trying, I know you can do it. I'll give you a secret." Daddy said. "For every sour thing you eat, you'll get more strength to pedal the bike!"
Daisy didn't understand what Daddy meant at first. But then, Daddy gave her a sour lolly. Daisy licked it, and it tasted sour. Suddenly, she felt stronger and was able to move the pedals. It worked!
Now Daisy is able to pedal her bike all by herself. She loves going for rides on it, and every once in a while Daddy reminds her to eat something sour for extra strength.
The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant. It was very strong, but it was very sad. One day a man came and put a tight chain around the the elephant's neck.
The man said, "Now, you will come with me and you have to do whatever I say!"
The elephant felt very sad and asked, "What do you want me to do?"
"Feed me! You have to feed me so I can stay strong!" the man said.
The elephant felt helpless and had no choice. It fed the man every single day without fail.
One day, the man's chain was too tight and the elephant became very angry. It pulled with all of its strength and broke the chain. The elephant ran away feeling happy and free.
The moral of the story is: never let anyone take advantage of you. Even if you feel helpless and there doesn't seem to be any way out, don't give up and fight for your freedom.

"Can we play with Spot, grandma?" Sara asks.
"Of course, dear. But be careful. He is very loud. He barks a lot. He might scare the birds," grandma says.
Sara and Ben nod. They take the ball and go to the garden. They throw the ball and Spot runs after it. He catches it and brings it back. He barks and jumps. He is loud. Sara and Ben laugh. They have fun.
But then, Spot sees a cat. The cat is on the fence. It is gray and fluffy. It has green eyes. Spot does not like the cat. He drops the ball and runs to the fence. He barks and growls. He is very loud. He tries to catch the cat.
"Spot, no!" Sara and Ben shout. They run after him. They want to stop him.
But the cat is fast. It jumps from the fence to the roof. It looks down at Spot. It hisses and spits. It is not afraid.
Spot is angry. He jumps and scratches the fence. He is very loud. He makes a hole in the fence. He goes through the hole. He chases the cat.
"Spot, come back!" Sara and Ben shout. They go through the hole. They follow him.
Grandma and grandpa hear the noise. They come out of the house. They see the hole in the fence. They see Sara and Ben running. They see Spot and the cat on the roof.
"Oh, no!" grandma and grandpa say. They are worried. They call Sara and Ben. They call Spot. They want them to come back.
But Sara and Ben do not hear them. They are too far. They are on the street. They see Spot and the cat on the roof of another house. They see a ladder. They climb the ladder. They want to get Spot and the cat.
But the ladder is old. It is weak. It breaks. Sara and Ben fall. They land on a pile of leaves. They are not hurt. But they are scared. They cry.
Spot and the cat hear them. They stop fighting. They look at them. They feel sorry. They come down from the roof. They go to them. They lick them. They are not loud. They are quiet.
Sara and Ben hug them. They are happy. They are not scared. They stop crying.
Grandma and grandpa find them. They are relieved. They hug them. They are glad. They are not angry. They smile.
They take them back to the house. They fix the fence. They give them cookies and milk. They read them the book. They are not loud. They are calm.
Sara and Ben say thank you. They say sorry. They say goodbye. They love their grandma and grandpa. They love Spot and the cat. They had a good visit. They will come back soon.

"Hello, Mr. Snowman!" Lily says. "We are happy to meet you."
"Yes, we are!" Ben says. "You are our new friend."
But then the sun comes out. It is very bright and warm. The snow starts to melt. Lily and Ben see that Mr. Snowman is getting smaller and smaller.
"Oh no!" Lily cries. "Mr. Snowman is going away!"
"Stop, sun, stop!" Ben shouts. "You are hurting Mr. Snowman!"
They run to Mr. Snowman and try to hug him. But he is too wet and cold. They feel sad.
"Mr. Snowman, we love you!" Lily says. "Please don't leave us!"
But Mr. Snowman cannot talk. He only smiles with his carrot nose. He wants to teach Lily and Ben something.
"Look, Lily, look, Ben," he says in his head. "I am not going away. I am changing. I am becoming water. Water is good. Water helps plants grow. Water makes rainbows. Water can be ice again. Maybe we can meet again. Don't be sad. Be happy."
Lily and Ben do not hear Mr. Snowman. But they feel something in their hearts. They feel a warm and happy feeling. They look at each other and smile.
"Maybe Mr. Snowman is right," Lily says. "Maybe he is not gone. Maybe he is just different."
"Yes, maybe he is," Ben says. "And maybe we can make him again. When it snows again."
They hold hands and walk away. They say goodbye to Mr. Snowman. They hope to see him again. They are happy.

"Wow, maybe this is treasure!" Tom said. "Let's open it and see what's inside."
Sam nodded. He saw a rock nearby and picked it up. He wanted to smash the lock with the rock. But Tom stopped him.
"Wait, Sam. Maybe this is not our box. Maybe someone else left it here. Maybe they will be sad if we break it. We should be kind and leave it alone."
Sam did not listen. He was too curious and excited. He said, "No, Tom. This is our box. We found it first. I want to see the treasure. Move away or I will hit you with the rock."
Tom was scared and sad. He did not want to fight with Sam. He did not want to hurt him or the box. He tried to talk to Sam, but Sam did not listen. He raised the rock and swung it at the lock.
But he missed. The rock hit the box and made a loud noise. The noise was like a beep. The box was not a box. It was a bomb. It was a bad bomb that someone left in the park. The bomb was ready to explode.
Tom and Sam did not know. They did not have time to run or hide. They did not have time to say sorry or hug. The bomb went off and made a big boom. The boom was very loud and very hot. It hurt Tom and Sam and the tree and the park. It was a very bad ending.

One day, a little bear and his mama went to look for honey in the forest. The little bear loved honey very much and wanted to eat it all the time. His mama told him to listen carefully and follow her, because there were many dangers in the forest.
"Listen, little bear, we have to be quiet and sneaky. There are big bees that guard the honey, and they can sting us if they see us. There are also other animals that like honey, and they can be mean and scary. Do you understand?" his mama said.
"Yes, mama, I understand. I will listen and follow you. I want to eat honey, but I don't want to get hurt or scared," the little bear said.
They walked and walked until they found a big tree with a hole in it. The little bear smelled honey and got very excited. He ran towards the tree, forgetting to listen and follow his mama. He stuck his head inside the hole and saw a lot of honey. He licked his lips and reached his paw inside.
But then he heard a terrible buzz. The big bees had seen him and were angry. They flew out of the hole and started to sting the little bear. The little bear cried out in pain and fear. He pulled his head and paw out of the hole, but it was too late. He was covered in stings and bumps.
His mama heard his cry and ran to help him. She scared away the bees and hugged the little bear. She licked his wounds and comforted him.
"I'm sorry, mama, I didn't listen and follow you. I was too greedy and foolish. The honey was not worth it. The bees were terrible and hurt me a lot," the little bear said.
"It's okay, little bear, I forgive you. You made a mistake, but you learned a lesson. Next time, you will listen and follow me, and we will find honey safely and happily. Now let's go home and rest. I love you, little bear," his mama said.
They walked back home, holding paws. The little bear felt sorry and sore, but also loved and grateful. He decided to listen and follow his mama from then on, and to share the honey with her and his friends. He realized that honey was sweet, but love was sweeter.

Anna liked to draw with her crayons. She had many colors and shapes on her paper. She was happy and proud of her art. But then she saw a big mistake. She had drawn a blue sun instead of a yellow one. She wanted to fix it, but she did not have a yellow crayon.
She looked around and saw an eraser on the table. It was enormous, bigger than her hand. She thought it could erase her blue sun. She grabbed it and rubbed it on her paper. But nothing happened. The blue sun was still there. She rubbed harder and harder, but the eraser did not work.
She was confused and sad. She asked her mom, who was sitting next to her. "Mom, why does this eraser not erase?" She showed her mom the eraser and the paper.
Her mom smiled and hugged her. "That is not an eraser, my dear. That is a sponge. It is for cleaning, not for erasing. It can make things wet, but not vanish. If you want to erase something, you need a different kind of eraser. Like this one." She gave Anna a small pink eraser that fit in her hand.
Anna tried the pink eraser on her paper. It worked! The blue sun vanished and left a white space. Anna was happy and thanked her mom. She found a yellow crayon and drew a new sun. She liked her art again. She learned that not all things that look like erasers are erasers. And that sometimes, mistakes can be fixed.

At the park, Tim and Sam found many circles. They saw a big round ball, a wheel on a bike, and a round cookie. Sam learned what a circle was and was happy. Tim and Sam played with the circles all day long.

Once upon a time there was an adorable little girl. She lived in the forest with her mother. Every day she would go outside to play.
One day, when she was walking in the forest, she found an axe. It was very shiny and looked very interesting. She wanted to carry it with her, so she did.
Suddenly, her mother saw her and yelled, "No! You can't carry an axe, it's too dangerous. Give it back now!"
The little girl shouted, "No! It's mine. I want to keep it!"
The mother said firmly, "No, you must return it. It is much too dangerous for a little girl like you."
The little girl sadly returned the axe and said, "I still want an axe, mommy."
Her mom smiled and said, "If I can find one for you, you can have it. But until then, you'll have to be safe."
The little girl nodded, and they went home together. And the little girl was more careful the next time she was walking in the forest.

The man tried to reverse the car again. Suddenly, the car started to move! But it went too fast. The car hit a tree and broke. The man was sad and Tim was sad too. They didn't know what to do. In the end, the car could not be fixed and the man had to walk home.

"Yes, it is. Do you want to make a snowman?" mom asks.

They laugh and hug the snowman. Then they see a hill with more snow.
"Can we climb the hill, mom?" Tom asks.
"Sure, but be careful. It might be slippery," mom says.
Tom and Mia run to the hill. They climb up and down. They slide on their bottoms. They throw snowballs at each other. They have fun.
"Wow, this is so cool!" Tom says.
"I'm cold and hungry," Mia says.
"Me too. Let's go inside," Tom says.
They run back to mom. She takes them inside. She makes them hot chocolate with marshmallows. She sprinkles some powder on top.
"What is this?" Mia asks.
"It's cinnamon. It makes the chocolate more yummy," mom says.
They sip their chocolate and eat some cookies. They feel warm and happy.
"Thank you, mom. You are the best," Tom and Mia say.
"You're welcome, my sweeties. I love you," mom says.
They hug and kiss mom. They finish their snack. They go to their room. They play with their toys. They tell each other stories. They fall asleep. They dream of snow and cinnamon.

Tim and Kim were curious. They liked to try new things. They asked Dad if they could try some spicy sauce. Dad said, "OK, but be careful. It might be very hot." He gave them each a small spoon. They dipped the spoon in the sauce. They put the sauce in their mouths.
Tim and Kim made a funny face. The sauce was very spicy. It burned their tongues. It made them cough. It made their eyes water. They did not like the sauce. They ran to the truck. They drank some water. They ate some apples. They felt better.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little rabbit named Remy. Remy loved to hop around and ask questions to all his friends in the forest. One sunny day, Remy found a big, orange carrot on the ground. He wanted to know who dropped the carrot, so he decided to ask his friends.
First, Remy hopped to his friend Sally the squirrel. "Sally, did you drop this carrot?" Remy asked. Sally shook her head and replied, "No, Remy, I did not drop the carrot. I like nuts, not carrots." Remy thanked Sally and continued his search.
Next, Remy went to see his friend Benny the bird. "Benny, did you drop this carrot?" Remy asked. Benny looked at the carrot and replied, "No, Remy, I did not drop the carrot. I like seeds, not carrots." Remy thanked Benny and hopped away.
Finally, Remy found his friend Tommy the turtle. "Tommy, did you drop this carrot?" Remy asked. Tommy smiled and replied, "Yes, Remy, I dropped the carrot. Thank you for finding it!" Remy gave the carrot back to Tommy, and they all played together for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Tom and Jerry. They always had fun outside and were best friends. One day, they were out playing in the woods. Suddenly, they heard a noise.

Tom looked scared and said, "Let's run away! We're not safe here!"
But Jerry took a deep breath and said, "No, we should help the mouse. It's not safe when the owl is fighting it."
So Tom and Jerry ran over and shouted at the owl. The owl flew away, and the mouse was safe!

They searched together. The little bird saw something red in the fog. "Is that your ball?" asked the bird. Spot ran to the red thing. It was his ball! "Thank you, little bird!" said Spot. They played together all day and became good friends.

The rabbit was jumping and hopping along, when he suddenly heard something behind him. He turned around and saw a tiny little mouse. The mouse said "Hi Peter Rabbit, why are you out this way?" Peter told the mouse his plan, and the mouse said "That sounds exciting!".
The mouse offered to join Peter on his long walk up the hill. Peter was excited, so the two of them began their journey up the hill.
As they kept walking, Peter began to get tired from all the hopping, but the mouse kept encouraging him. Finally, they reached the top of the hill and saw the most beautiful view. The sun was setting, and Peter was so happy.
Peter Rabbit and the Mouse decided to have a picnic, and enjoyed the special moment. Peter wanted to remember this special day, and now he does every time he looks up at the long hill.

One day, she saw a big, black dog with a red collar. It looked scary and angry. It barked loudly and ran towards Lily and her dad. Lily was afraid and wanted to run away.
But her dad was wise. He told her to stay calm and not to scream. He said, "Lily, don't worry. The dog is just playing. He won't hurt us. We just need to be friendly and gentle. Look, he has a name tag. His name is Max. Can you say hi to Max?"
Lily listened to her dad and tried to be brave. She said, "Hi, Max. You are a big dog. Do you like to jog too?" The dog stopped barking and wagged his tail. He licked Lily's hand and sniffed her dad's leg. He seemed happy and friendly.
Lily smiled and petted the dog. She said, "You are a nice dog, Max. I like you. Do you have a home?" The dog nodded and pointed his nose to a house nearby. There was a man standing at the door. He waved and said, "Sorry, I'm Max's owner. He escaped from the room when I opened the door. He loves to jog and chase things. He didn't mean to scare you. He's a good boy."
Lily's dad said, "It's okay. We're not scared. We like Max. He's a good jogger. Maybe we can jog with him again sometime." The man said, "Sure, that would be great. Come on, Max. Let's go back to the room. Say bye to Lily and her dad." Max barked and wagged his tail. He said bye to Lily and her dad and followed his owner to the house.
Lily and her dad continued to jog in the park. They felt happy and safe. They learned that sometimes scary things are not so scary after all. They just need to be wise and friendly.

But one day, a big wind came and blew away all the food. The animals were sad and scared. The wise, hairy cat told them not to worry. She said that the wind was a test for them. The cat told them to use their wisdom and imagine a way to find more food.
The animals thought hard and came up with a plan. They worked together to find more food and shared it with everyone. In the end, the animals learned that they could overcome any problem if they used their wisdom and worked together.

One day, a furry cat named Kitty went for a walk. Kitty saw a door with a shiny knob. The door was open a little bit. Kitty was curious and wanted to see what was behind the door.
Kitty pushed the door open and went inside. It was very cold! Kitty started to shiver and shake. The room was so cold that Kitty began to freeze. Kitty knew she had to find a way to get warm again.
Kitty saw a big, soft blanket on the floor. She ran to the blanket and wrapped herself in it. The blanket was warm and cozy. Kitty was happy and not cold anymore. She learned to stay away from the cold room with the shiny knob.

One day, Tom and Sue were playing in the yard. Tom had a big ball and Sue had a little doll. They were very happy. The sun was shining and the birds were singing.
Suddenly, Tom kicked the ball too hard and it hit Sue's doll. The doll's arm broke. Sue was very sad and cried. "You broke my doll! That's bad!" she said. Tom felt bad too. He wanted to find a way to make Sue happy again.
Tom had an idea. He ran inside the house and brought out a cup of juice. He gave it to Sue and said, "I'm sorry I broke your doll. Here's some juice to make you feel better." Sue stopped crying and took a sip of the juice. But it was not just any juice. It was magic juice! As soon as Sue drank it, her doll's arm was fixed! Sue and Tom were both very surprised and happy. They played together all day, and from then on, they were more careful with their toys.

One day, a nosy cat named Tim saw a big red ball. The ball had the word "zoom" on it. Tim was very curious about the ball. He wanted to play with it, but the ball was in a tall tree. Tim tried to jump and reach it, but he could not.
A small bird named Sue saw Tim trying to get the ball. Sue flew up to the tree and said, "I can help you get the ball. I will give it to you." Tim was happy and said, "Thank you, Sue!" Sue flew to the top of the tree and pushed the ball down.
The ball fell from the tree and went "zoom" on the ground. Tim chased after the ball, laughing and having fun. Sue watched from the tree, happy to see her new friend play. Tim and Sue became best friends, and they played with the zoom ball every day.

Anna was a big girl who wanted to go to university. She liked to learn new things and read many books. She had a brown bag where she kept her pencils and papers. She dreamed of going to a big school where she could study more and make new friends.
One day, her mother told her that they had to move to another town. Anna was very sad and angry. She did not want to leave her home and her friends. She did not want to go to a new school where she did not know anyone. She cried and cried and said, "I don't want to go! I want to stay here and go to university!"
Her mother hugged her and said, "I know, my dear, I know. But sometimes we have to do things that we don't like. We have to move because daddy got a new job. He will work hard to save money for us. And you can still go to university when you grow up. You can study anywhere, as long as you have your brown bag and your books. And you can make new friends in the new school. They will like you because you are smart and kind."
Anna wiped her tears and looked at her mother. She felt a little better. She said, "OK, mommy, I will try. But can I keep my brown bag and my books?"
Her mother smiled and said, "Of course, my dear, of course. They are yours. And you can always write to your old friends and visit them someday. Now, let's pack your things and get ready to go. We have a big adventure ahead of us."
Anna nodded and hugged her mother. She still felt sad, but she also felt brave. She knew that she could face the change and still follow her dreams. She learned that sometimes we have to cry, but we also have to try.
The moral value of the story is: We should be adaptable and resilient when we face challenges or changes in life. We should not give up on our goals or our friends, but we should also be open to new opportunities and experiences.

The girl was so happy to have her toy and the rag back. Tim felt proud that he could help the girl find her toy and make her happy.

Lily heard Tom's cry and ran to him. She saw the blood on his leg and felt scared. But she wanted to help her brother. She took off her scarf and wrapped it around his wound. She hugged him and said, "Don't cry, Tom. I'm here. I'll comfort you."

Lily smiled back and said, "I love you too, Tom. Come on, let's go home. Mom will make it better."
They left the axe and the apples behind and walked home, holding hands. They learned a lesson that day. Axes are not for children. And sisters are for comforting.
